rulings.model: The IRS test uses age when the care was provided: "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled." The restatement uses age at the end of 2025 (≥ 13), so it checks the box for a disabled child who turned 13 in 2025 but got care only while 12. It also never checks the box for a disabled person who is not a dependent only because "The disabled person had gross income of $5,200 or more" (or filed a joint return, or you could be claimed as a dependent), and no refusal names those cases.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: second construction right in part; proposed finding (the box changes no amount). i2441 p. 3, Column (c): "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled." After BUG-0080 the project checks the box for a qualifying person 13 or older at the end of 2025 who was not able to care for themselves. For a disabled child who turned 13 during 2025 and whose care in 2025 was all given before the 13th birthday, no care was provided while the child was over age 12, so the box should be clear; the project checks it, and asks nothing that tells care before the birthday from care after it (`dependent.dc_under13` asks only whether the child was under 13 for part of the time the care was paid for). The transcription ruling on 2(c) (the project's reading: checked) rests on care given after the birthday, while the child was over 12 and disabled; it does not reach this case. Proposed fix: for a person aged 13 at the end of 2025, check the box only when some of the care was provided on or after the 13th birthday (one question), or accept the box as checked for every disabled child who turned 13 as a display reading for the owner. The model's second point is project retained, refusal located elsewhere: a disabled person who would be your dependent but for gross income of $5,200 or more, a joint return or your being claimable (i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s), item 3, "or could claim as a dependent except: a. The disabled person had gross income of $5,200 or more, b. The disabled person filed a joint return, or c. You (or your spouse if filing jointly) could be claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's 2025 tax return") is refused through f2441.nondependent_gate on lines 2 and 3 (f2441.qp_count, f2441.paid_total), so such a person is never listed. Kept as encoded pending the owner (handoffs/HANDOFF-STAGE-15.md, question 15): the fix asks when the care was given, a new input.
